title: KOReader API token is committed before plugin zip generation can fail

evidence.quote:
if not PLUGIN_TEMPLATE_DIR.exists() or not PLUGIN_TEMPLATE_DIR.is_dir():
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
            detail="KOReader plugin template is not available on the server.",

except ValueError as exc:
                    raise HTTPException(
                        status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                        detail="KOReader plugin settings template is invalid.",

api_token = APIToken(
        user_id=current_user.id,
        name=payload.token_name,
        token_hash=token_hash,
        token_prefix=token_prefix,
    )
    session.add(api_token)
    session.commit()

    zip_bytes = _build_plugin_zip(server_url=server_url, api_token=raw_token)

reasoning: If the template directory is missing or the settings template is invalid, the endpoint returns 500 after creating and committing a live API token. The caller never receives the raw token, so the account accumulates active, unrecoverable credentials.
reproduction: Temporarily remove the KOReader template directory or its required placeholders, then POST `/api/plugins/koreader/download` as an authenticated user. The response fails, but an unrevoked `APIToken` row has already been committed.
recommendation: Build the zip before committing the token, or wrap token creation and zip generation in a transaction and roll back on any packaging failure. Commit only once the response payload is ready to send.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: `tests/test_plugins.py` covers the successful packaging path and missing-auth path, but not template failure after token creation.
suggestedRegressionTest: Mock `_build_plugin_zip` to raise and assert no active APIToken is persisted for the requesting user.
